positions.position: the classification covers minor or major impurity, usually prompted by illness or travel; it names the junub case and details ordinary and incidental causes for the other
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 (author): The classification covers minor or major impurity, usually prompted by illness or travel; it names the junub case and details ordinary and incidental causes for the other.

positions.position: alternatively, “prayer” means its locations, the mosques; the point is to forbid excessive drinking and drunkenness rather than a drunk person approaching prayer
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 (author): Alternatively, “prayer” means its locations, the mosques; the point is to forbid excessive drinking and drunkenness rather than a drunk person approaching prayer.

positions.position: alternatively, the phrase describes junub people, meaning “other than those passing through.”
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 (author): Alternatively, the phrase describes junub people, meaning “other than those passing through.”

positions.position: the exception is evidence that tayammum does not remove the state of ritual impurity
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 (author): The exception is evidence that tayammum does not remove the state of ritual impurity.

positions.position: al-zajjāj defines ṣaʿīd as the face of the earth, whether soil or another surface
positions.reasons: NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 (الزجاج): Al-Zajjāj defines ṣaʿīd as the face of the earth, whether soil or another surface.

positions.position: the min in the corresponding phrase in 5:6 marks the starting point, not a partitive meaning
positions.reasons: NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 (author): The min in the corresponding phrase in 5:6 marks the starting point, not a partitive meaning. | mentions 5:6

positions.position: the community agrees that a person who mistakenly utters a word of disbelief is not judged an unbeliever
positions.reasons: NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 (author): The community agrees that a person who mistakenly utters a word of disbelief is not judged an unbeliever.

positions.position: the noun سُكر can also mean a dam or blockage, while سَكر means an intoxicating substance that prevents discernment
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The noun سُكر can also mean a dam or blockage, while سَكر means an intoxicating substance that prevents discernment.

positions.position: ibn jinnī analyzes غيط as فعيل from غيط, analogizing it to هين and سيد when reduced
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (ابن جني): Ibn Jinnī analyzes غيط as فعيل from غيط, analogizing it to هين and سيد when reduced.

positions.position: abū ḥayyān says غيط is properly فعل, like غوط, because arabic uses both غاط يغوط and غاط يغيط; غوط pluralizes as أغواط
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): Abū Ḥayyān says غيط is properly فعل, like غوط, because Arabic uses both غاط يغوط and غاط يغيط; غوط pluralizes as أغواط.

positions.position: the verb تغوط means to relieve oneself; غاط في الأرض means to sink until hidden from view
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The verb تغوط means to relieve oneself; غاط في الأرض means to sink until hidden from view.

positions.position: the address is to sober people: the intoxicated person lacking discernment is not then addressed, but upon sobering must fulfill duties missed while intoxicated
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The address is to sober people: the intoxicated person lacking discernment is not then addressed, but upon sobering must fulfill duties missed while intoxicated.

positions.position: requiring the sober person to make up duties does not impose the impossible, despite the contrary position held by some
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): Requiring the sober person to make up duties does not impose the impossible, despite the contrary position held by some.

positions.position: the command calls for prayer in its proper form, joining sincere worship of god with good conduct toward other people
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The command calls for prayer in its proper form, joining sincere worship of God with good conduct toward other people.

positions.position: لا تقربوا الصلاة is stronger than لا تصلوا وأنتم سكارى: forbidding approach to prayer intensifies the prohibition
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): لا تقربوا الصلاة is stronger than لا تصلوا وأنتم سكارى: forbidding approach to prayer intensifies the prohibition.

positions.position: abū ḥayyān calls al-ḍaḥḥāk’s and ʿubayda’s readings weak and remote; al-qurṭubī says they are sound in meaning because distractions diminish attentiveness
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): Abū Ḥayyān calls al-Ḍaḥḥāk’s and ʿUbayda’s readings weak and remote; al-Qurṭubī says they are sound in meaning because distractions diminish attentiveness.

positions.position: the apparent meaning forbids approaching prayer while intoxicated
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The apparent meaning forbids approaching prayer while intoxicated.

positions.position: another view takes the command as a prohibition of intoxication itself, since prayer is obligatory but drunkenness is unpredictable
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (قيل): Another view takes the command as a prohibition of intoxication itself, since prayer is obligatory but drunkenness is unpredictable.

positions.position: the amount of drink that causes drunkenness varies by quantity and temperament, so avoiding wine protects prayer observance
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (قيل): The amount of drink that causes drunkenness varies by quantity and temperament, so avoiding wine protects prayer observance.

positions.position: the majority read سكارى with ḍamma on س; grammarians debate whether it is a broken plural or a collective noun
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الجمهور): The majority read سكارى with ḍamma on س; grammarians debate whether it is a broken plural or a collective noun.

positions.position: sībawayh explicitly classifies سكارى as a broken plural on the فعالى pattern used for adjectives
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (سيبويه): Sībawayh explicitly classifies سكارى as a broken plural on the فعالى pattern used for adjectives.

positions.position: ibn al-badhish mistakenly attributes to sībawayh the view that سكارى is a collective noun, which he considers analogically plausible
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (ابن الباذش): Ibn al-Badhish mistakenly attributes to Sībawayh the view that سكارى is a collective noun, which he considers analogically plausible.

positions.position: abū ḥayyān corrects ibn al-badhish: sībawayh explicitly says it is a broken plural and distinguishes noun-patterns from adjective plurals
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): Abū Ḥayyān corrects Ibn al-Badhish: Sībawayh explicitly says it is a broken plural and distinguishes noun-patterns from adjective plurals.

positions.position: al-sīrāfī records both analyses and prefers the broken-plural parsing, which agrees with sībawayh
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (السيرافي): Al-Sīrāfī records both analyses and prefers the broken-plural parsing, which agrees with Sībawayh.

positions.position: the emphatic construction parallels prohibitions against approaching adultery, indecencies, and an orphan’s property
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The emphatic construction parallels prohibitions against approaching adultery, indecencies, and an orphan’s property. | mentions 17:32, 6:151, 6:152

positions.position: a group reads سكارى with fatḥa on س, as a broken plural analogous to ندمان and ندامى
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (فرقة): A group reads سكارى with fatḥa on س, as a broken plural analogous to ندمان and ندامى.

positions.position: the phrase means do not come to prayer
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The phrase means do not come to prayer.

positions.position: some supply an omitted noun, “the places of prayer,” making this a prohibition on entering mosques
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (قيل): Some supply an omitted noun, “the places of prayer,” making this a prohibition on entering mosques.

positions.position: the places intended are mosques, supported by a prophetic report instructing that children and madmen be kept from mosques
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The places intended are mosques, supported by a prophetic report instructing that children and madmen be kept from mosques.

positions.position: ʿubayda al-salmānī interprets it as needing to urinate, citing the prohibition on praying while holding urine and a version about compressing one’s thighs
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (عبيدة السلماني): ʿUbayda al-Salmānī interprets it as needing to urinate, citing the prohibition on praying while holding urine and a version about compressing one’s thighs.

positions.position: some early authorities, including the ḥanafī school, define legally relevant drunkenness as inability to distinguish a man from a woman
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (جماعة من السلف): Some early authorities, including the Ḥanafī school, define legally relevant drunkenness as inability to distinguish a man from a woman.

positions.position: al-thawrī defines drunkenness as mental disturbance, such as garbling recitation and speaking without knowing what one says
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الثوري): Al-Thawrī defines drunkenness as mental disturbance, such as garbling recitation and speaking without knowing what one says.

positions.position: aḥmad, and similarly mālik, regard a person as drunk when his mind changes from its sober state
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (أحمد ومالك): Aḥmad, and similarly Mālik, regard a person as drunk when his mind changes from its sober state.

positions.position: some infer that drinking was initially permitted in early islam until it produced drunkenness
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (قيل): Some infer that drinking was initially permitted in early Islam until it produced drunkenness.

positions.position: al-qaffāl suggests that stimulating drinks that encouraged generosity, courage, and zeal may have been allowed, but deliberate use of mind-destroying drink was not
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (القفال): Al-Qaffāl suggests that stimulating drinks that encouraged generosity, courage, and zeal may have been allowed, but deliberate use of mind-destroying drink was not.

positions.position: al-qaffāl adds that if someone unintentionally drank enough to lose reason, the legal burden was lifted from him
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (القفال): Al-Qaffāl adds that if someone unintentionally drank enough to lose reason, the legal burden was lifted from him.

positions.position: janāḥ ibn ḥubaysh transmits كسلى with either ḍamma or fatḥa, as al-zamakhsharī relates
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (جناح بن حبيش): Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh transmits كسلى with either ḍamma or fatḥa, as al-Zamakhsharī relates.

positions.position: the phrase means until you recover and understand what you say; it names the intended result, since an intoxicated person does not understand speech
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The phrase means until you recover and understand what you say; it names the intended result, since an intoxicated person does not understand speech.

positions.position: al-zamakhsharī also permits an adjectival parse: the restriction concerns junub residents without an excuse
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhsharī also permits an adjectival parse: the restriction concerns junub residents without an excuse.

positions.position: to explain prayer while junub in travel, al-zamakhsharī paraphrases the phrase as not washed until washing, except when traveling
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الزمخشري): To explain prayer while junub in travel, al-Zamakhsharī paraphrases the phrase as not washed until washing, except when traveling.

positions.position: the majority prohibit junub men and menstruating women from reciting any qurʾān until washing. mālik permits a short protective verse and permits a menstruant to recite freely if she fears forgetting
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الجمهور): The majority prohibit junub men and menstruating women from reciting any Qurʾān until washing. Mālik permits a short protective verse and permits a menstruant to recite freely if she fears forgetting.

positions.position: the endpoint keeps a junub person from prayer until the whole body has been washed
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The endpoint keeps a junub person from prayer until the whole body has been washed.

positions.position: ʿaṭāʾ and al-ḥasan reportedly require washing even if the person dies; abū ḥayyān answers with the report of ʿamr ibn al-ʿāṣ at dhāt al-salāsil, whose tayammum after fearing death was approved by the prophet
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (عطاء والحسن): ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḥasan reportedly require washing even if the person dies; Abū Ḥayyān answers with the report of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ at Dhāt al-Salāsil, whose tayammum after fearing death was approved by the Prophet.

positions.position: ʿaṭāʾ, al-zuhrī, mujāhid, mālik, al-awzāʿī, al-layth, al-shāfiʿī, and muḥammad ibn jarīr do not make either act obligatory in either purification
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (عطاء والزهري ومجاهد ومالك والأوزاعي والليث والشافعي ومحمد بن جرير): ʿAṭāʾ, al-Zuhrī, Mujāhid, Mālik, al-Awzāʿī, al-Layth, al-Shāfiʿī, and Muḥammad ibn Jarīr do not make either act obligatory in either purification.

positions.position: the verse names washing without stating an intention requirement; abū ḥanīfa and his companions do not require intention for water purification
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (أبو حنيفة وأصحابه): The verse names washing without stating an intention requirement; Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions do not require intention for water purification.

positions.position: mālik's well-known position, al-shāfiʿī, aḥmad, isḥāq, and abū thawr require intention; al-walīd ibn muslim transmitted the contrary view from mālik
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (مالك والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور): Mālik's well-known position, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, and Abū Thawr require intention; al-Walīd ibn Muslim transmitted the contrary view from Mālik.

positions.position: al-shāfiʿī and the listed authorities hold that any bodily contact with a woman's body invalidates purity
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الشافعي وابن مسعود وابن عمر والزهري وربيعة وعبيدة والشعبي وإبراهيم ومنصور وابن سيرين): Al-Shāfiʿī and the listed authorities hold that any bodily contact with a woman's body invalidates purity.

positions.position: al-awzāʿī says contact invalidates ablution when it is by hand, but not otherwise
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الأوزاعي): Al-Awzāʿī says contact invalidates ablution when it is by hand, but not otherwise.

positions.position: if water is too scarce to use without risking thirst, the majority permit tayammum
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الجمهور): If water is too scarce to use without risking thirst, the majority permit tayammum.

positions.position: for the majority any travel allows the concession, whether or not it qualifies for shortening prayers; other jurists require a shortening journey, and another group requires travel for obedience
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الجمهور): For the majority any travel allows the concession, whether or not it qualifies for shortening prayers; other jurists require a shortening journey, and another group requires travel for obedience.

positions.position: another view treats someone beyond hearing people's voices as being like a traveler
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (قيل): Another view treats someone beyond hearing people's voices as being like a traveler.

positions.position: the pure reading is illustrated by the verse describing those whom the angels take as ṭayyibīn, meaning purified from disobedience
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The pure reading is illustrated by the verse describing those whom the angels take as ṭayyibīn, meaning purified from disobedience. | mentions 16:32

positions.position: aḥmad and abū yūsuf limit material to soil and sand; most jurists allow saline earth except ibn rāhawayh
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (أحمد وأبو يوسف): Aḥmad and Abū Yūsuf limit material to soil and sand; most jurists allow saline earth except Ibn Rāhawayh.

positions.position: abū ḥayyān summarizes al-zamakhsharī's answer as justifying the early mention of illness and travel because they are more frequent and first deserving of a concession
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): Abū Ḥayyān summarizes al-Zamakhsharī's answer as justifying the early mention of illness and travel because they are more frequent and first deserving of a concession.

positions.position: abū ʿubayda and al-farrāʾ define ṣaʿīd as soil
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (أبو عبيدة والفراء): Abū ʿUbayda and al-Farrāʾ define ṣaʿīd as soil.

positions.position: one group takes ṭayyib as pure; abū ḥanīfa and mālik hold this, and al-ṭabarī chooses it, as in the description of the dead as pure from stains of disobedience
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (أبو حنيفة ومالك والطبري): One group takes ṭayyib as pure; Abū Ḥanīfa and Mālik hold this, and al-Ṭabarī chooses it, as in the description of the dead as pure from stains of disobedience.

positions.position: abū ḥayyān says the sound reports clarify the location and manner of wiping that the verse leaves open to possibility
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): Abū Ḥayyān says the sound reports clarify the location and manner of wiping that the verse leaves open to possibility.

positions.position: some jurists permit not tracing the creases of the face
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): Some jurists permit not tracing the creases of the face.

positions.position: abū ḥayyān calls the starting-point reading strained: arabs understand مسحت برأسه من الدهن والماء والتراب as partitive, and he approves yielding to truth over disputation
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): Abū Ḥayyān calls the starting-point reading strained: Arabs understand مسحت برأسه من الدهن والماء والتراب as partitive, and he approves yielding to truth over disputation.

positions.position: the cited line continues with the question of how a youth intoxicated by both love and wine could recover
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): The cited line continues with the question of how a youth intoxicated by both love and wine could recover.

positions.position: the root’s general meaning is obstruction: it describes sleep clouding a hawk’s eye and a river ceasing to flow
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): The root’s general meaning is obstruction: it describes sleep clouding a hawk’s eye and a river ceasing to flow.

positions.position: repeating لا marks a separate prohibition for each state; prohibition under both states together is still stronger and more fitting
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): Repeating لا marks a separate prohibition for each state; prohibition under both states together is still stronger and more fitting.

positions.position: the cited verse uses جنابة in the sense relevant to the term جنب
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): The cited verse uses جنابة in the sense relevant to the term جنب.

positions.position: جنب has one form for singular, dual, plural, masculine, and feminine because it behaves like the verbal noun الإجناب
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhshari explains that جنب has one form for singular, dual, plural, masculine, and feminine because it behaves like the verbal noun الإجناب.

positions.position: some arabs also inflect جنب: dual جنبان, sound plural جنبون, and broken plural أجناب, like شلل
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): Some Arabs also inflect جنب: dual جنبان, sound plural جنبون, and broken plural أجناب, like شلل.

positions.position: العبور means passage; ناقة عبر الهواجر in the cited poetry attests the usage
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): العبور means passage; ناقة عبر الهواجر in the cited poetry attests the usage.

positions.position: منكم is an adjective of أحد in the nominative, attached to an omitted element; من الغائط attaches to جاء as its object
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): منكم is an adjective of أحد in the nominative, attached to an omitted element; من الغائط attaches to جاء as its object.

positions.position: ibn masud reads الغيط; ibn jinni analyzes it as a shortened فيعل form, like هين and ميت
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (ابن مسعود): Ibn Masud reads الغيط; Ibn Jinni analyzes it as a shortened فيعل form, like هين and ميت.

positions.position: a second analysis treats الغيط as a verbal noun, with dialect forms غاط يغيط غيطا and غاط يغوط غوطا
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (غير مسمى): A second analysis treats الغيط as a verbal noun, with dialect forms غاط يغيط غيطا and غاط يغوط غوطا.

positions.position: abu al-baqa calls الغيط a verbal noun of يغوط and explains its yāʾ as substituted wāw; the author objects that he missed the distinct yāʾ dialect
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (أبو البقاء): Abu al-Baqa calls الغيط a verbal noun of يغوط and explains its yāʾ as substituted wāw; the author objects that he missed the distinct yāʾ dialect.

positions.position: the فَ in فتيمموا is the response to the condition
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): The فَ in فتيمموا is the response to the condition.

positions.position: وجد here means لقي and therefore takes one object
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): وجد here means لقي and therefore takes one object.

positions.position: صعيدا is the direct object of تيمموا, meaning ‘intend’; the proposed analysis with an omitted preposition is not a valid analogy
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): صعيدا is the direct object of تيمموا, meaning ‘intend’; the proposed analysis with an omitted preposition is not a valid analogy.

positions.position: a further reading سكارى with fatḥa on sīn and alif is a broken plural, by analogy with ندمان/ندامى and عطشان/عطاشى
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (غير مسمى): A further reading سكارى with fatḥa on sīn and alif is a broken plural, by analogy with ندمان/ندامى and عطشان/عطاشى.

positions.position: the majority read سكارى with damma on sīn and alif; the author prefers analyzing it as a broken plural, as sibawayh does
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (الجمهور): The majority read سكارى with damma on sīn and alif; the author prefers analyzing it as a broken plural, as Sibawayh does.

positions.position: ibn al-badhish attributes to sibawayh the alternative analysis that سكارى is a collective noun, arguing no plural pattern has this form
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (ابن الباذش): Ibn al-Badhish attributes to Sibawayh the alternative analysis that سكارى is a collective noun, arguing no plural pattern has this form.

positions.position: al-sirafi records the disagreement and favors analyzing سكارى as a broken plural
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (السيرافي): Al-Sirafi records the disagreement and favors analyzing سكارى as a broken plural.

positions.position: al-zamakhshari reports جناح بن حبيش’s paired forms كسلى/كسلى, with the kāf rounded and open, as comparable adjective usage
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhshari reports جناح بن حبيش’s paired forms كسلى/كسلى, with the kāf rounded and open, as comparable adjective usage.

positions.position: sa'd reports that after an anṣari hosted and served wine to migrants and anṣar, they became drunk and boastful; a man struck sa'd's nose with a camel jaw, and the verse then descended before wine
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (سعد بن أبي وقاص): Sa'd reports that after an Anṣari hosted and served wine to migrants and Anṣar, they became drunk and boastful; a man struck Sa'd's nose with a camel jaw, and the verse then descended before wine was prohibited. Muslim transmits the full report; other Sunan collections transmit it except Ibn Majah.

positions.position: the best definition of intoxication is being unable to know what one is saying; drunkenness muddles recitation and removes reflection and humility
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (author): The best definition of intoxication is being unable to know what one is saying; drunkenness muddles recitation and removes reflection and humility.

positions.position: other authorities allow menstruating and postpartum women to pass if they can avoid contamination, and otherwise forbid passage
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (بعض الأئمة): Other authorities allow menstruating and postpartum women to pass if they can avoid contamination, and otherwise forbid passage.

positions.position: ibn abbas says men used to come to prayer drunk before wine was prohibited; abu razin and mujahid give the same explanation, and ibn jarir transmits it
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says men used to come to prayer drunk before wine was prohibited; Abu Razin and Mujahid give the same explanation, and Ibn Jarir transmits it.

positions.position: ibn jarir prefers wine intoxication and says the command addresses someone capable of understanding responsibility, not one so drunk that he cannot understand speech, who is legally like an insane person
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (ابن جرير): Ibn Jarir prefers wine intoxication and says the command addresses someone capable of understanding responsibility, not one so drunk that he cannot understand speech, who is legally like an insane person.

positions.position: the legal address applies to one who understands speech, since understanding is a condition of legal responsibility; several legal theorists state this principle
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (author): The legal address applies to one who understands speech, since understanding is a condition of legal responsibility; several legal theorists state this principle.

positions.position: the verse may indirectly prohibit intoxication altogether: a regular drinker cannot consistently perform the five daily prayers at their times; ibn kathir compares this to the exhortation to prepare to die muslim in 3:102
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (author): The verse may indirectly prohibit intoxication altogether: a regular drinker cannot consistently perform the five daily prayers at their times; Ibn Kathir compares this to the exhortation to prepare to die Muslim in 3:102. | mentions 3:102

positions.position: al-khattabi says several scholars weaken the prohibition report because aflat ibn khalifa is unknown
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (أبو مسلم الخطابي): Al-Khattabi says several scholars weaken the prohibition report because Aflat ibn Khalifa is unknown.

positions.position: abu zur'a says the commonly cited route through jasra from umm salama is incorrect; the sound attribution is jasra from aisha
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (أبو زرعة الرازي): Abu Zur'a says the commonly cited route through Jasra from Umm Salama is incorrect; the sound attribution is Jasra from Aisha.

positions.position: al-thawri says habib narrated only from urwa al-muzani; yahya al-qattan calls the report nearly worthless, and bukhari weakens it because habib did not hear from urwa
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (الثوري): Al-Thawri says Habib narrated only from Urwa al-Muzani; Yahya al-Qattan calls the report nearly worthless, and Bukhari weakens it because Habib did not hear from Urwa.

positions.position: yahya al-qattan calls the report nearly worthless
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (يحيى القطان): Yahya al-Qattan calls the report nearly worthless.

positions.position: bukhari weakens the report because habib ibn abi thabit did not hear from urwa
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (البخاري): Bukhari weakens the report because Habib ibn Abi Thabit did not hear from Urwa.

positions.position: ibn majah’s version names urwa ibn al-zubayr; ahmad’s route through hisham ibn urwa explicitly supports that identification, while another abu dawud route names urwa al-muzani, leaving the attribution uncertain
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (author): Ibn Majah’s version names Urwa ibn al-Zubayr; Ahmad’s route through Hisham ibn Urwa explicitly supports that identification, while another Abu Dawud route names Urwa al-Muzani, leaving the attribution uncertain.

positions.position: abu hanifa limits sa‘id to materials of the soil kind, including earth, sand, arsenic, and lime
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (أبو حنيفة): Abu Hanifa limits sa‘id to materials of the soil kind, including earth, sand, arsenic, and lime.

positions.position: al-shafi‘i, ahmad, and their followers restrict sa‘id to soil, citing quran 18:40, where it means smooth bare earth
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (الشافعي وأحمد بن حنبل وأصحابهما): Al-Shafi‘i, Ahmad, and their followers restrict sa‘id to soil, citing Quran 18:40, where it means smooth bare earth. | mentions 18:40

positions.position: ibn abbas says the best earth is cultivated soil; ibn abi hatim transmits this and ibn mardawayh raises it to the prophet in his tafsir
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says the best earth is cultivated soil; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits this and Ibn Mardawayh raises it to the Prophet in his tafsir.

positions.position: al-shafi‘i supports wiping the face and arms with a report from ibn al-simma that the prophet performed tayammum by wiping his face and arms
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (ابن الصمة): Al-Shafi‘i supports wiping the face and arms with a report from Ibn al-Simma that the Prophet performed tayammum by wiping his face and arms.

positions.position: the ibn al-simma report describes the prophet scraping a wall with a stick, striking it with his hand, and wiping his face and arms
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (ابن الصمة): The Ibn al-Simma report describes the Prophet scraping a wall with a stick, striking it with his hand, and wiping his face and arms.

positions.position: usayd told aisha that god had turned every disliked matter that befell her into good for her and the muslims
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (أسيد بن الحضير): Usayd told Aisha that God had turned every disliked matter that befell her into good for her and the Muslims.

positions.position: an absolute ruling is restricted by a qualified one when that is its only basis; examples include just witnesses, inheritances after bequest or debt, believing-slave expiation, ablution, and blood restricted to flowing blood
positions.reasons: BURHAN, d. 794 (author): An absolute ruling is restricted by a qualified one when that is its only basis; examples include just witnesses, inheritances after bequest or debt, believing-slave expiation, ablution, and blood restricted to flowing blood.

positions.position: the verse names passing excrement as the evident, necessary cause of purification; sleep and other cases are left implicit and inferred
positions.reasons: BURHAN, d. 794 (author): The verse names passing excrement as the evident, necessary cause of purification; sleep and other cases are left implicit and inferred.

positions.position: some prohibitions target a state or attribute rather than the act itself: do not die except as muslims means avoid dying outside islam, like the example about praying only in humility
positions.reasons: BURHAN, d. 794 (author): Some prohibitions target a state or attribute rather than the act itself: do not die except as Muslims means avoid dying outside Islam, like the example about praying only in humility.

positions.position: tawriya subtly evokes one of a word’s meanings while intending another; istikhdām employs both meanings together, each cued by a separate contextual indicator
positions.reasons: BURHAN, d. 794 (author): Tawriya subtly evokes one of a word’s meanings while intending another; istikhdām employs both meanings together, each cued by a separate contextual indicator.

positions.position: the two-fatḥa class contains 16 forms across 29 places; the list includes جاء أحد منكم, جاء أجلهم, جاء أمرنا, جاء آل, جاء أحدهم, and شاء أنشره
positions.reasons: NASHR, d. 833 (author): The two-fatḥa class contains 16 forms across 29 places; the list includes جاء أحد منكم, جاء أجلهم, جاء أمرنا, جاء آل, جاء أحدهم, and شاء أنشره.

positions.position: ḥamza, al-kisāʾī, and khalaf read without alif in both places; the others read with alif
positions.reasons: NASHR, d. 833 (author): Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read without alif in both places; the others read with alif. | mentions 5:6

positions.position: the address means those who profess belief in the messengers and what they brought from god; the foremost duty is to avoid associating anything with him
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): The address means those who profess belief in the messengers and what they brought from God; the foremost duty is to avoid associating anything with Him.

positions.position: the arabic root sense of intoxication is blocking a path
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): The Arabic root sense of intoxication is blocking a path.

positions.position: the travel concession applies to short trips as well as long ones
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): The travel concession applies to short trips as well as long ones.

positions.position: the description ṭayyib is illustrated by the verse saying that good land brings forth its plants by its lord’s permission
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): The description ṭayyib is illustrated by the verse saying that good land brings forth its plants by its Lord’s permission. | mentions 7:58

positions.position: tayammum is a distinctive act of worship granted to this community
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): Tayammum is a distinctive act of worship granted to this community.

positions.position: the prohibition also bars conduct approaching the sin of an intoxicated tongue uttering words unworthy of god
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): The prohibition also bars conduct approaching the sin of an intoxicated tongue uttering words unworthy of God.

positions.position: tayammum alleviates the otherwise severe restriction when using water is difficult or impossible
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): Tayammum alleviates the otherwise severe restriction when using water is difficult or impossible.

positions.position: ʿafw means that god leaves punishment for the offense, especially the error made while intoxicated
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): ʿAfw means that God leaves punishment for the offense, especially the error made while intoxicated.

positions.position: the restriction on junub remains until the body has been deliberately washed
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): The restriction on junub remains until the body has been deliberately washed.

positions.position: the verse orders concessions from the cases most in need of them toward those less in need, beginning with illness and travel
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): The verse orders concessions from the cases most in need of them toward those less in need, beginning with illness and travel.

positions.position: ibn abbas says a sexually impure person may not approach prayer when water is available; without water, tayammum by wiping the earth is permitted
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL, d. 911 (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says a sexually impure person may not approach prayer when water is available; without water, tayammum by wiping the earth is permitted.

positions.position: mujahid says the illness clause was revealed about an anṣārī man too ill to rise for ablution and without a helper; he brought the problem to the prophet
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL, d. 911 (مجاهد): Mujahid says the illness clause was revealed about an Anṣārī man too ill to rise for ablution and without a helper; he brought the problem to the Prophet.

positions.position: ibn abbas, through ata al-khurasani, says “prayer” here refers to the mosques
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL, d. 911 (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas, through Ata al-Khurasani, says “prayer” here refers to the mosques.

positions.position: mujahid says a person with smallpox or similar illness may omit ablution, adding that this is among the quran's difficult interpretations
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL, d. 911 (مجاهد): Mujahid says a person with smallpox or similar illness may omit ablution, adding that this is among the Quran's difficult interpretations.

positions.position: mujahid says al-ghaʾit means a valley
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL, d. 911 (مجاهد): Mujahid says al-ghaʾit means a valley.

positions.position: ubayda demonstrated his interpretation to muhammad ibn sirin by closing his fingers as if grasping something
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL, d. 911 (عبيدة): Ubayda demonstrated his interpretation to Muhammad ibn Sirin by closing his fingers as if grasping something.

positions.position: ibn abbas says the best earth for tayammum is cultivated land
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL, d. 911 (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says the best earth for tayammum is cultivated land.

positions.position: qatada says pure earth is land with no trees or vegetation
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL, d. 911 (قتادة): Qatada says pure earth is land with no trees or vegetation.

positions.position: ibn abd al-barr says the incident occurred during the banu al-mustaliq campaign; ibn sa'd and ibn hibban preceded him, while some later scholars object because of the locations aisha names
positions.reasons: ITQAN, d. 911 (ابن عبد البر): Ibn Abd al-Barr says the incident occurred during the Banu al-Mustaliq campaign; Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Hibban preceded him, while some later scholars object because of the locations Aisha names. | mentions 4:43

positions.position: abu ubayd al-bakri locates al-bayda as the rise before dhu al-hulayfa on the mecca road, and dhat al-jaysh a day's post from medina
positions.reasons: ITQAN, d. 911 (أبو عبيد البكري): Abu Ubayd al-Bakri locates al-Bayda as the rise before Dhu al-Hulayfa on the Mecca road, and Dhat al-Jaysh a day's post from Medina. | mentions 4:43

positions.position: al-ṣalah can refer to places of prayer
positions.reasons: ITQAN, d. 911 (author): Al-ṣalah can refer to places of prayer.

positions.position: different explanations reported from companions for one verse can reflect different readings rather than disagreement
positions.reasons: ITQAN, d. 911 (author): Different explanations reported from Companions for one verse can reflect different readings rather than disagreement.

positions.position: gabriel told the prophet that ibn ʿabbas would become the community’s learned authority, and the prophet was to treat him well
positions.reasons: ITQAN, d. 911 (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Gabriel told the Prophet that Ibn ʿAbbas would become the community’s learned authority, and the Prophet was to treat him well.

positions.position: ibn ʿabbas reports the prophet told him, “you are an excellent interpreter of the quran.”
positions.reasons: ITQAN, d. 911 (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet told him, “You are an excellent interpreter of the Quran.”

positions.position: ibn masʿud calls ʿabd allah ibn ʿabbas the interpreter of the quran
positions.reasons: ITQAN, d. 911 (ابن مسعود): Ibn Masʿud calls ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas the interpreter of the Quran.

positions.position: mujahid says ibn ʿabbas was called “the ocean” because of the extent of his knowledge
positions.reasons: ITQAN, d. 911 (مجاهد): Mujahid says Ibn ʿAbbas was called “the ocean” because of the extent of his knowledge.

positions.position: ibn al-hanafiyya calls ibn ʿabbas the learned authority of the community
positions.reasons: ITQAN, d. 911 (ابن الحنفية): Ibn al-Hanafiyya calls Ibn ʿAbbas the learned authority of the community.

positions.position: al-hasan recounts ʿumar’s praise of ibn ʿabbas as a young man among elders, with an inquisitive tongue and discerning heart
positions.reasons: ITQAN, d. 911 (الحسن): Al-Hasan recounts ʿUmar’s praise of Ibn ʿAbbas as a young man among elders, with an inquisitive tongue and discerning heart.

positions.position: the prohibition says not to approach prayer, though its intent is not to perform it while intoxicated, emphasizing the warning
positions.reasons: BURSEVI, d. 1127 (author): The prohibition says not to approach prayer, though its intent is not to perform it while intoxicated, emphasizing the warning.

positions.position: prayer is the believer’s ascension and appointed time for intimate conversation with god; the worshipper is one who converses with his lord
positions.reasons: BURSEVI, d. 1127 (author): Prayer is the believer’s ascension and appointed time for intimate conversation with God; the worshipper is one who converses with his Lord.

positions.position: a worshipper should guard prayer from distractions that occupy the heart and purify the self from defilement, pursuing the highest attainable purification
positions.reasons: BURSEVI, d. 1127 (author): A worshipper should guard prayer from distractions that occupy the heart and purify the self from defilement, pursuing the highest attainable purification.

positions.position: some say the prohibition concerned only praying in congregation with the prophet, to honor him; al-alusi rejects this as unsupported by transmission or reason and contrary to the apparent text and occasion
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (بعضهم): Some say the prohibition concerned only praying in congregation with the Prophet, to honor him; al-Alusi rejects this as unsupported by transmission or reason and contrary to the apparent text and occasion.

positions.position: al-shihab, quoting al-bahr and abd al-qahir, distinguishes a simple state adjective from a clause stating that the people were intoxicated independently
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (الشهاب): Al-Shihab, quoting al-Bahr and Abd al-Qahir, distinguishes a simple state adjective from a clause stating that the people were intoxicated independently.

positions.position: al-subki applies the distinction to a vow of retreat while fasting: صائما requires a fast for that vow, whereas وأنا صائم requires concurrence and is fulfilled during ramadan
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (السبكي): Al-Subki applies the distinction to a vow of retreat while fasting: صائما requires a fast for that vow, whereas وأنا صائم requires concurrence and is fulfilled during Ramadan.

positions.position: anas reports that the prophet told a drowsy worshipper to leave, sleep, and return when he knows what he is saying; a similar report is attributed to aisha
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (أنس): Anas reports that the Prophet told a drowsy worshipper to leave, sleep, and return when he knows what he is saying; a similar report is attributed to Aisha.

positions.position: the sleep interpretation is somewhat far-fetched, and combining sleep and wine intoxication is still less plausible because it mixes literal and metaphorical senses without a clear indicator
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): The sleep interpretation is somewhat far-fetched, and combining sleep and wine intoxication is still less plausible because it mixes literal and metaphorical senses without a clear indicator.

positions.position: the prohibition targets the state of intoxication while the duty to pray remains; the qualifying state is the object of negation, and the general prayer obligation is not cancelled
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): The prohibition targets the state of intoxication while the duty to pray remains; the qualifying state is the object of negation, and the general prayer obligation is not cancelled.

positions.position: al-jassas states that if intoxication spans the whole prayer time, the person still must make up the prayer
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (الجصاص): Al-Jassas states that if intoxication spans the whole prayer time, the person still must make up the prayer.

positions.position: ali reports that after wine at abd al-rahman ibn awf's feast, the intoxicated companions put him forward and he misrecited al-kafirun; al-tirmidhi calls the report hasan and al-hakim authenticates it
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (علي): Ali reports that after wine at Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf's feast, the intoxicated Companions put him forward and he misrecited al-Kafirun; al-Tirmidhi calls the report hasan and al-Hakim authenticates it.

positions.position: another report from ali says abd al-rahman led the people in the maghrib prayer, while wine was still permitted
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (علي): Another report from Ali says Abd al-Rahman led the people in the Maghrib prayer, while wine was still permitted.

positions.position: the vocative and attention marker introduce the rule with special emphasis
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): The vocative and attention marker introduce the rule with special emphasis.

positions.position: intoxication is the settled state produced by drinking wine; its root conveys closure or obstruction, as in the phrase about eyes being sealed
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): Intoxication is the settled state produced by drinking wine; its root conveys closure or obstruction, as in the phrase about eyes being sealed.

positions.position: al-jassas says entry is not allowed unless the water or the route is in the mosque
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (الجصاص): Al-Jassas says entry is not allowed unless the water or the route is in the mosque.

positions.position: until you wash marks the end of the prohibition on approaching prayer in janaba; placing the exception first signals that this rule is not absolute, unlike the intoxication rule
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): Until you wash marks the end of the prohibition on approaching prayer in janaba; placing the exception first signals that this rule is not absolute, unlike the intoxication rule.

positions.position: another explanation says washing is mentioned, though not the main point of validity while junub, to show that janaba ends only through ritual washing

positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): The verse signals that worshippers should avoid distractions and purify the self; if the body must be purified, purifying the heart is even more fitting, since it is God's throne.

positions.position: those passing along a path are interpreted as travelers

positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): Scholars disagree whether tayammum removes ritual impurity; on close inspection this verse proves neither position.

positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (قيل): Another view takes ʿafw here to mean facilitation, citing the Prophet's statement that he waived alms on horses and slaves.

positions.reasons: ELMALILI, d. 1361 (author): Elmalılı says there is no need to depart from salat's basic meaning: an intoxicated person who cannot understand his words cannot pray validly, and intoxication is forbidden.

positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): The author describes semantics and rhetoric as especially useful, after legal foundations, for discerning God’s intent, interpreting ambiguities, uncovering subtleties, and recognizing inimitability.

positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (عبد القاهر): ʿAbd al-Qahir warns that interpreters who take metaphorical or illustrative wording literally corrupt its meaning and purpose and obscure its eloquence.

positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): Immersion in Arabic sermons, poems, proverbs, customs, and conversation gives later learners a taste analogous to native instinct; taste perceives eloquent speech’s qualities.

positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (السكاكي): Al-Sakkaki says an outsider may imitate an expert’s judgments when taste is lacking until time and study supply it.

positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): Poetry and Arab usage clarify difficult meanings and persuade learners; rhetoric, beyond grammatical rules, reveals meanings and can tip a choice between interpretations.

positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): Mention of janāba is an embedded transition to the new rule of tayammum, since the requirement of ritual bathing was already established.

positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): Tayammum was instituted during the campaign of al-Muraysīʿ, in either year five or six AH according to the preferred chronology.
